sessions.description: In this session, Albert Tort, Secretary of Telecommunications and Digital Transformation of the Generalitat de Catalunya, and Maria Galindo, Secretary for Digital Policies of the Government of Catalonia, will explain Catalunya's plan to invest €1 billion in artificial intelligence by 2030 — and what it means for everyone building AI from Barcelona. Expect a concrete view of how startups, enterprises and researchers can plug into the strategy — and why Catalunya intends to become the place where European AI gets built.

sessions.title: Keynote 2 - The Hidden Blockers to Autonomous Operations
sessions.description:
Autonomous AI agents promise to revolutionize enterprise operations, moving beyond simple chat interfaces to execute complex, multi-step business workflows. Yet, despite massive investments in state-of-the-art LLMs, most enterprise agent pilots hit a hard wall when deployed into real-world operational environments. They loop endlessly, act on stale batch data, bypass security controls, or trigger cascade failures across critical backend systems.

The problem isn't the intelligence of the model; it's the fragmentation of the underlying enterprise architecture.

In this session, Avinash Jha explores why autonomous agents collapse without a Unified Information Fabric. Drawing from real-world enterprise failure modes, this talk breaks down the critical infrastructure gaps, from legacy API boundaries to unmonitored tool execution and presents a pragmatic blueprint for bridging AI reasoning with enterprise execution.

Key Takeaways:

The Enterprise Integration Gap: Why traditional, deterministic API gateways fail when handling non-deterministic, agentic execution loops and dynamic prompt streams.

The Three-Tier Gateway Topology: How to complement existing API Gateways with AI/LLM Gateways (for model routing, streaming, and token cost controls) and MCP Gateways (for agent tool discovery, runtime context, and kill-switch governance).

Zero-Trust Identity for Agents: How to replace high-privilege service accounts with task-scoped, short-lived cryptographic tokens to prevent runaway agent actions.

The Unified Fabric Blueprint: A step-by-step architectural framework to connect real-time event streams, model context protocols, and legacy systems of record into a resilient foundation for autonomous operations.

sessions.title: Panel 1 - Beyond the Pilot: Making Enterprise AI Pay Off

sessions.title: Workshop 1 - The Ultra-Scale Talk: Scaling Training to Thousands of GPUs
sessions.description: Training large language models demands more than raw compute. it requires a deep understanding of parallelism and architecture choices. This talk dives into the practicalities of ultra-scale training: how 5D parallelism makes it possible to stretch a single run across massive GPU clusters, how Mixture-of-Experts architectures introduce new scaling dimensions and stability challenges, and the performance tuning and communication patterns that drive throughput. Drawing from the Ultra-Scale Playbook and real-world scaling efforts, we'll cover benchmarks, hard-earned lessons, and hands-on recommendations for engineers and researchers ready to train state-of-the-art models efficiently!

sessions.title: Workshop 2 - When code is cheap, governance is the hard part
sessions.description:
The Challenge 

Code generation is close to free now. Review, sign-off, and audit are not, and that gap lands squarely on engineering leaders. In this session, I'll show you where AI-generated changes actually fail before production, and how automated checks and audit trails hold humans and AI to the same standard without slowing releases.

What You'll Do & Take Away 

Hands-on from minute five, you will take a repository, ask an AI agent to change it, and close the loop. You'll put your standards where the agent reads them by wiring a live rules check into the agent's own turn over MCP, making it fix its own violations before the code reaches you.

By the end, you leave with a working repository, the configuration, and a reusable skill running on the AI coding tool of your choice.

Who Should Attend 

Anyone who writes code with an AI tool, and anyone who has to sign it off.

What to Bring & How to Prepare

Primary Setup: Bring a laptop with a browser and a free GitHub account. The repository opens directly in GitHub Codespaces, so there is nothing to install, and a free AI coding account is enough for every task.

Power Users: If you already use Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Replit, or another MCP client, feel free to bring that instead.

No Laptop? No Problem: Every step is demonstrated live on screen, and pairing with the person next to you works fine. The repository stays public so you can redo everything afterwards on your own time.

sessions.title: Keynote 4 - Gen AI: Myths and Reality
sessions.description:
Despite what you might think from reading the news since late 2022,
Artificial Intelligence did not appear with ChatGPT. This
"Revolution" is merely the fruit of a long maturation, spanning
several decades. After a brief historical review, we'll delve into
these new AIs, the Generative AIs. We'll look at their limits and
potential, and how they can be used for good or ill. Finally, we'll
try to understand what the prospects are for us, humans, and for
these technologies.

sessions.title: Demo 2 - Satellites, Planes, Trains: Why Hardware's Cursor Moment Just Started
sessions.description: Claude and Cursor are already transforming how software is written: accelerating development, augmenting engineers, and collapsing the gap between idea and implementation. Hardware is next. I'd like to talk about how AI-augmented systems engineering will do for complex physical systems design (satellites, airplanes, trains) what these tools are doing for code: turning months of fragmented, document-heavy engineering work into a fluid, intelligent process. This isn't speculative: the foundations are being built now. At Systellar, we've developed Synapse™ specifically to bring AI into the core of how complex hardware programs are designed, traced, and validated. My talk will explore what this transformation looks like, why hardware has been harder to crack than software, and what the future of engineering looks like when AI becomes a genuine design partner and, eventually, completely transforms the industry into an agentic one.

sessions.title: Keynote 6 - Moving beyond Productivity: How Enterprise AI Creates Organizational Impact at Scale
sessions.description:
AI is taking hold in the enterprise — and yet many organizations are still waiting for the payoff. The tools are powerful. The potential is real. But something fundamental is missing between individual productivity and lasting organizational impact.
In this session, we explore some of the challenges and dive into three concrete themes that shape the next chapter of enterprise AI: how generative UI shifts enterprise software from navigation to intent; how company memory grounds agents in organizational context; and how tabular AI democratizes business predictions. Actionable, opinionated and anchored in product truth.

sessions.title: Panel 2 - Rebuilding the Org Chart: What Actually Breaks When Enterprises Restructure Around AI
sessions.description: Every enterprise AI rollout eventually stops being a technology project and becomes an org design problem. Job descriptions written for execution, teams built around headcount, managers measured on output that agents now produce. This panel goes at the structural rebuild: which roles get redrawn, where the reporting lines break, what upskilling actually costs, and why leadership readiness fails before the tooling does. Enterprise transformation leads and an operator scaling a company through it, on what they had to dismantle before anything worked.

sessions.title: Demo 4 - I Built Autonomous GTM Engines - So Can You.
sessions.description:
​Most companies bolt AI onto their old GTM playbook. It never gets them there.

​The modern GTM stack is one engine.

Your data and your know-how feed one shared brain, the brain powers the apps your team uses every day, a human checks anything important before it goes out.

Chaos in, playbooks out.

​In this live session, David Arnoux walks through how he builds this inside real companies, from B2B software scale-ups to consumer brands.

What you'll take away

​What a GTM OS actually is, and why bolting AI onto the old playbook fails,

​The core components of the engine: signals, workflows, agents and reporting in one shared brain,

​How the engine progresses from reactive → proactive → autonomous

​Real builds from both worlds. A €2.5B B2B software company and consumer brands running programmatic SEO at 12,000+ pages

​What it takes to build a GTM OS inside your company in days, not months, and why roughly 80% of each new build carries over to the next.

sessions.title: Panel 3 – AI Act × AI Value Chain and Governance
sessions.description: The AI Act is not one obligation, it's a chain of them, and everyone in the chain is writing contracts to push them downstream. Then Article 25 reshuffles the deck: rebrand a system, modify it, or change what it's for, and you become the provider. Lawyers and governance leads on where liability actually lands between model providers, integrators and deployers, where the regulation is clear, and where it leaves you carrying risk you never priced.

sessions.title: Workshop 3 - Why and how to build a personal brand on LinkedIn with AI, the right way (one of the few moats left)
sessions.description:
AI made building things easy. So, what's actually left to compete on?

This session argues it's brand, trust, and human relationships. Three things AI can't clone from a screenshot, and all three take time to build.

Google's Zero Moment of Truth research points to 7 hours and 11 touch points before someone trusts you enough to buy. In this session, we break down what that looks like in B2B today, and we zoom in on LinkedIn specifically.

Give AI the right context, and it can actually help you build brand, trust, and relationships. Skip that step and you get slop. We'll build the context live, on stage, with a volunteer from the audience. One person, their real business.

Jacob Zangel and Charlie Hills dig into who they are, what they stand for, their ICP, and what actually sets them apart from the competition.

Only once that's on the table does AI get involved in helping them create content for LinkedIn. We might even create a post (or two), live. You leave knowing what you need to feed AI so it can actually help you, instead of handing you slop.

⚠️ Important! Who is this for?

B2B founders, execs, marketers, and builders already posting on LinkedIn consistently, at least once or twice a week over the past few months.

You want to see how Charlie Hills grew a following of 250K+ on LinkedIn, 70K newsletter subscribers, and over 100M organic lifetime impressions. We'll show you all the different parts of his LinkedIn AI OS, and demonstrate live how some of the core parts actually work.

If you're not posting yet, or not posting consistently, this session won't be the best use of your time.

What you'll walk away with:

→ The few moats left in B2B, and why building a personal brand is the one you can start on Monday
→ The 2026 B2B buying math: why "88 touches across 10 stakeholders" replaced the old advice to just be everywhere, and what that means for your content plan
→ The context that makes AI useful, not slop: watch us pull it out of a volunteer live, ICP, positioning, differentiation, before we start creating any content with AI

sessions.title: Workshop 4 - Give Your Product a Voice — Build a Live AI Voice Agent in 60 Minutes
sessions.description:
Everyone's talking about voice AI. In this room, you'll actually ship one.

Roshan and Barbara will get you from a blank screen to a working, talking AI agent that can hold a real phone conversation, before the coffee break ends. You'll design its personality, wire up its brain (LLM), give it ears and a mouth (speech-to-text and text-to-speech), and connect it to a real tool so it does more than chat, it acts.

Bring a laptop and an idea. Leave with a deployed agent, a live phone number, and the know-how to build the next one yourself.

What you'll walk away with:
• A working voice agent you built yourself, live
• A mental model for the voice AI stack (STT → LLM → TTS → tools) and where the real engineering challenges hide (latency, interruption handling, tool-calling reliability)
• The gap between a slick demo and something that survives a real caller — the practical lessons Vapi's forward-deployed engineers see across production deployments

Best for: builders, PMs, and founders who want to stop reading about voice AI and start shipping it. No ML background required — bring curiosity and a laptop.

Discover how to use AI to govern AI, creating a centralized "Command Center" that provides visibility into costs, security, and PII without slowing down your engineering teams. Open source demo.

sessions.title: Keynote 14 - AI, Rewired: Building Edge Intelligence That Adapts, Distributes and Acts

sessions.description:

Streaming Architecture: A comprehensive walkthrough of a robust, cloud-native architecture using Azure Databricks, Event Hubs, and Unity Catalog for secure and scalable data ingestion.

sessions.title: Keynote 16 - Learning Is the New Infrastructure. Most Companies Haven't Built It Yet.
sessions.description: Most AI workforce transformations fail not because of the technology, but because organisations cannot absorb change at speed. Christian Rebernik draws on 25 years of building at scale, as CTO and Managing Director at N26, founder of the digital health platform Vivy, and cofounder of Tomorrow University of Applied Sciences, to argue that learning is the defining infrastructure challenge of the AI era. Every company has rolled out AI. Almost none have changed how they work. This session gives CEOs, CHROs and anyone deploying AI inside an organisation a concrete framework: what a learning organisation actually looks like, why training programmes structurally cannot deliver it, and the three conditions that separate organisations that absorb change from those that only announce it. Using Tomorrow University as a live case study, Christian shows what this looks like in practice, and the one question leaders can ask their own teams this week.

sessions.title: Panel 5 - Strategic Money: How Corporates Really Invest in AI Startups
sessions.description: Corporate venture money isn't chasing the same thing as a fund. A strategic investor wants synergy, access, and an eventual seat at the table, not just a return. This panel brings together the people who sit between corporates and startups to unpack how strategic AI investments and partnerships actually get picked, structured and managed: what a corporate is really underwriting beyond the cap table, where that clashes with how independent VCs think, and what founders get wrong pitching a corporate as if it were a fund. Built for founders courting strategic capital and for anyone trying to understand how big companies actually move on AI.

sessions.title: Keynote 19 - Going beyond vibes with genuinely useful evals
sessions.description: Move beyond gut checks with evaluations that measure what actually matters. Build reliable feedback loops to improve quality, catch regressions, and ship with confidence.

sessions.title: Keynote 18 - The AI Operating Model Advantage: Why Winning with AI Requires Rewiring the Organization
sessions.description:
AI is everywhere, but enterprise-wide impact remains elusive. The reason is increasingly clear: most companies are putting powerful new technology into organizations designed for a pre-AI world. They automate tasks, add copilots and deploy agents, while leaving the underlying workflows, decision rights and management structures largely untouched.

The next wave of AI value will come from changing that. For industrial companies in particular, AI creates an opportunity to rethink not only individual tasks, but how expertise, decisions and work flow across the enterprise.

This session will explore why AI winners are moving beyond productivity to redesign their operating models around AI: concentrating on the few domains where AI can create strategic advantage, rewiring end-to-end workflows rather than bolting AI onto existing processes, and building organizations in which humans and AI agents work together at a fundamentally different speed and scale.

The future of AI is human.

sessions.title: Keynote 21 - The magic of turning human brainwaves into art with AI

sessions.title: Keynote 20 - Train Once, Recommend Forever: Recsys for an Ever-Growing Catalog
sessions.description:
Modern consumer products all share one trait: their catalog never stops growing. Streaming platforms, news feeds, marketplaces — new titles, articles, and listings arrive every day, and users expect to see them in their recommendations right away. But recommender systems learn exclusively from past user interactions, so an item that just arrived, with no interaction history yet, is invisible to them by design. The traditional fix is to retrain continuously — and that's exactly the trap: it couples what a system can recommend to when it was last trained.

In this talk we follow the paradigm shift now reshaping recommender systems: decoupling a model's training from what it's allowed to recommend. Starting from the transformers that power modern discovery, we show why they cannot represent new items, how content embeddings almost solve the problem — and where they fall short — and how the approach we built at Albatross and run in production behind every feed, closes the gap: new items recommendable within minutes, retraining almost never, and quality above the ID-based baseline. Everything backed by production-scale experiments.

sessions.title: Use Case 1 - Product Discovery is finally solved: Introducing Perception Models
sessions.description:
Large marketplaces and ecommerce have a discovery problem that traditional recommendation systems were not built to solve: every item is unique, catalogs change rapidly, and metadata is inconsistent. Hundreds of thousands of new listings enter the catalog every day with no impressions or interaction history - effectively invisible to legacy systems. The result is a discovery experience that remains static as users browse, click, and refine their interests, while newly listed items can take days to surface.

Albatross has solved this problem with perception models. This new class of AI learns from live user behavior, understands user intent in real time, and reshapes discovery as each session unfolds - while every new unique item becomes immediately discoverable.

In this talk, we will also explore live deployments and in particular our partnership with Wallapop, one of the first C2C marketplaces globally to move toward in-session, adaptive discovery that understands user intent as it unfolds, and advancing user engagement and seller visibility at unprecedented scale.

sessions.title: Panel 6 - Physical AI: Humanoids, Robot Fleets & Europe's Hardware Gap
sessions.description: Physical AI is 2026's breakout story: humanoids leaving the lab, LLM-driven robot fleets, and a hardware race Europe is losing to China. Can the EU build, not just regulate?

sessions.title: Keynote 23 - AI made it easy. Who decides what's good?
sessions.description:
As AI rapidly generates designs, code, content, and recommendations, many organizations are focused on speed and efficiency. But when outputs are cheap and abundant, speed alone is no longer a competitive advantage. The real challenge becomes defining what good work actually looks like.
This talk reframes “good” in the AI era as outcomes, not outputs. Drawing on Sense & Respond thinking, it treats AI-generated artifacts as a new class of assumptions—powerful, persuasive, and requiring validation. AI doesn’t eliminate uncertainty; it accelerates our ability to create hypotheses. The work of teams is still to decide which assumptions matter and how to test them.

Attendees will learn why managing to outcomes becomes more critical as AI increases throughput, and how AI tools can be used to generate, test, and invalidate ideas faster—strengthening learning loops rather than replacing judgment.

“Good” in the AI era is not about adopting tools. It’s about building organizations that learn faster than their assumptions.

sessions.title: Demo 10 - Demo of AI co-Workers to augment pharma commercial teams
sessions.description:

We are building an AI-native agentic layer that helps reps work 10 times faster, increases HCP engagement 5 times, and gives doctors and pharmacists trusted 24/7 access to pharma companies.

sessions.description: Discover the fascinating evolution of artificial intelligence, from its theoretical foundations in the 1940s to the generative AI revolution of 2026. sessions.title: Panel 7 - Healing or Hooking? AI's Double Edge on Mental Health & Wellbeing
sessions.description: Same AI, two opposite stories. On one side: AI therapy companions making mental health support 24/7 and accessible, mood-tracking that catches a crisis early, mindfulness coaches in your pocket, generative tools that help people process trauma. On the other: recommendation systems wired to maximise screen time, dopamine engineering disguised as engagement, attention economies that reward outrage, and AI companions that quietly replace human connection. Where does the line sit between AI helping us thrive and AI hooking us into something that costs more than it gives? Builders, clinicians and behavioural scientists argue out what 'wellbeing' should actually mean in an algorithmic world — and who pays the bill when it goes wrong.

sessions.title: Keynote 25 - Gravity Always Wins: Why Profitable Efficient Growth is the Path to Victory, Especially In The Era of AI
sessions.description: A practical session on how founders and GTM leaders can define what “winning” actually looks like in an AI-native world. Sam will break down the milestones, KPIs, and decision points that matter most as companies scale beyond early traction, helping leaders understand where to focus, what signals to trust, and how to make smarter growth decisions in rapidly changing markets.

sessions.title: Demo 11 - The Agent Was the Easy Part: Putting an AI Analyst in Front of a Whole Company
sessions.description:
AirHelp is a flight-compensation company with a small data team and a wide
variety of data-hungry stakeholders, all asking the same kind of question:
"what was X last month, split by Y?" We put an AI analyst — AIDA — into Slack
so the whole company could ask directly.

The talk is about the part that isn't the agent. We deliberately did not
build text-to-SQL. AIDA cannot write a query against the warehouse. It can
only compose answers from metrics a human has already defined, tested and
version-controlled in our semantic layer. That constraint is the product.
Text-to-SQL demos work on stage and fail in production, because no warehouse
is self-describing and the model does not know what your company means by
"active customer".

I'll cover the architecture, real examples of how it changed the way people
get answers day to day, and the culture shift it forced — inside the data
team, where the job moved from answering questions to defining what the
answers mean, and outside it, where people had to learn what a governed
answer is and when the system should say no.

The takeaway for anyone leaving to build this on Monday: your agent is a
function of your definitions. Spend the money there.

sessions.title: Use Case 3 - AI Voice Agents: From Pilot to Production
sessions.description:
Voice AI has left the lab. Enterprises are putting AI voice agents in front of real customers, and the gap between a promising pilot and a production deployment is where many projects stall.

Drawing on deployments across multiple industries, we'll examine what it takes to run voice agents at enterprise scale: the barriers that most often derail adoption, the technical foundations production demands (real-time latency, accuracy on real-world audio, predictable cost), and the operational groundwork that separates a compelling demo from a system customers rely on.

Attendees will leave with a clear view of how leading companies moved from proof of concept to production, the mistakes that cost them time, and a practical framework for deploying voice AI that holds up in live customer conversations.

sessions.title: Workshop 7  - Token Compression and Routing, how to control agentic coding costs
sessions.description:
First, you make it work. Then you make it efficient.
We've spent the last two years proving that LLMs can write code, run agents, and orchestrate complex workflows. Today, Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and others are the modern platforms for executing computational tasks, and tokens represent their new bandwidth.

Token compression is about using that bandwidth wisely and accounting for costs from an engineering perspective.

This is a hands-on session on the key techniques and a framework for reasoning about this as a fundamental property of the systems you ship, not an afterthought. Attendees will leave with concrete actions they can implement this week, and a mental model for thinking about token efficiency as a compounding infrastructure advantage rather than a line-item cost.

sessions.title: Workshop 8 - Building Your Second Brain
sessions.description: You leave this room with a second brain of your own: a personal knowledge base your AI can actually read. Answer any question about your team or your last twelve months at work in under a minute, sources attached. Start the day with an empty inbox instead of 128 unread emails. Build a deck from your own notes in two hours instead of two days. This is not a demo. You install the tools, connect your first sources and write a skill that runs before you leave, and you walk out with a folder structure, your first knowledge files and something already working for you. Bring a laptop, ideally with Cursor, Obsidian or Claude installed in advance.

sessions.title: Keynote 26 - AI & Education
sessions.description: To be announced...

sessions.title: Hands-On Workshop: Building Agents with Google Antigravity (Bring Your Laptop), by Google Cloud
sessions.description: Step into the future of autonomous software engineering in this 90-minute hands-on lab challenge. Take command with Google Antigravity as you solve real-world tasks - moving from rapid terminal refactoring to orchestrating autonomous multi-agent swarms that execute tools, browse the web, and build software alongside you. (Please bring your laptop!)

sessions.title: Demo 12 - When anyone can build, the person who decides WHAT to build becomes the bottleneck
sessions.description:
Building got cheap. Deciding what deserves to be built did not.

At Bricks I shipped production AI agents acting as product builder with coding agents as teammates. I could move faster than ever but I quickly realized that my ability to judge whether what I had just built was actually right dropped. 

This talk is field notes from that gap. What breaks when delivery outruns judgment. Why stuffing more context into agents makes them try to satisfy everything and what I think builders need to change now, whether you’re a PM, an engineer, or a founder watching your team figure out who owns what.

sessions.title: Use Case 4 - Efficiency? Not only. A new way of working and delivering value to customers
sessions.description: Ecoembes and NTT DATA share what happened when an efficiency programme turned into a change in how teams actually work. Starting from a familiar goal — do the same things faster — the first results forced a rethink of the development model, team structures and the business–technology relationship, built on SPECs, spec-driven and test-driven development, and AI. The freed capacity raised a harder question: what becomes possible that wasn't viable before? A real-world account of simplifying and personalising customer interactions, and the scaling challenges — measurement, security, governance, model cost, architecture.

sessions.title: Panel 8 - Retail Rewired: AI from Storefront to Checkout
sessions.description: From demand forecasting and dynamic pricing to AI stylists, smart inventory, and a checkout that knows you before you reach it — retail is being rebuilt aisle by aisle. And now agents are starting to shop on the customer's behalf, forcing brands to rethink who they're really selling to. Retail and e-commerce operators on what AI is already changing on the shop floor and online, and what breaks when real customers and real margins are on the line.

sessions.title: Keynote 27 - The era of useful, secure AI business software
sessions.description: 2026 was the era of shiny demos and prototypes. 2027 will be the era of useful, secure business software that powers your business operations. This talk unveils how the next generation of business apps will be built by non-technical teams - not because we simplified code, but because we simplified creation.

sessions.title: Debate 2 — Future of Work: Will AI Replace Half of Knowledge Workers by 2030?
sessions.description: Tobi Lütke told Shopify managers: don't hire unless you can prove AI can't do the job. Goldman estimated it as a $7-trillion global GDP boost. Wall Street is pricing in the productivity surge. So is this the great unbundling of the knowledge economy — or the latest in a 30-year history of tech-replaces-work predictions that never came true? Two debaters fight it out: one sees a near-future where the white-collar middle is hollowed out, the other sees AI as the most powerful augmentation tool we've ever built, with employment levels intact. 55 minutes, bell-to-bell.

sessions.title: Demo 13 - Cursed Apps: Building (and Breaking) the ChatGPT × Claude Ecosystem
sessions.description:
ChatGPT Apps and Claude Connectors are quietly becoming a new app layer built on top of AI assistants — but almost nobody has stress-tested what these platforms can actually do, or where they break.

This talk opens with a live build: crafting a working app from scratch on Skybridge, an open-source framework for shipping apps that run inside both ecosystems. From there it gets weird. Drawing on a set of deliberately useless experiments built to probe the limits of the MCP App ecosystem, the talk walks through what happens when ChatGPT users and Claude users fight for territory on a shared pixel canvas; rival AI models get dropped into one group call together; a cadavre exquis has players each draw one section of a picture without ever seeing the whole; a game of telephone pictionary degrades — beautifully — across LLM sessions; and independent AI agents try to coordinate through pheromone trails, ant-colony style.

None of these are products. They're stress tests — and what breaks, and what doesn't, says more about where this ecosystem actually stands than any roadmap slide could.

sessions.title: Use Case 5 - Engineering Production Agents: The Model Is the Easy Part
sessions.description: Building an impressive agent prototype is increasingly easy. Making it reliable, responsive and economically viable in production is much harder. In this session, Dylan Bristot unpacks that gap through real Nebius Token Factory use cases: how Revolut scaled AI agents across financial crime and customer support, and how Sword Health made a much larger reasoning model responsive enough for its AI wellbeing specialist. A short live demo turns those lessons into a practical framework for model choice, inference architecture, observability and cost.

sessions.title: Panel 9 - Women Who Lead the Room: Closing AI's Leadership Gap
sessions.description: AI is rewriting who gets heard, funded and promoted. Founders and leaders on building inclusive AI leadership pipelines — and why visibility is the new currency.

sessions.title: Demo 14 - The Hiring Debt Nobody Talks About
sessions.description: How people infrastructure debt accumulates silently in the early stage, and what it actually costs founders when it catches up with them.

sessions.title: Use Case 6 - When Every AI Company Sounds the Same: How to Build and Prove Real Differentiation
sessions.description:
In an AI market where nearly every company makes similar claims, genuine differentiation is increasingly difficult to articulate and even harder to prove. Using Maisa’s experience as the central case study, David Villalón and Manu Romero will discuss how founders can build a defensible position through fundamental technology choices, measurable customer outcomes and the ability to meet the highest standards of trust, security and accountability.

The session will explore what distinguishes a compelling narrative from a truly differentiated company, particularly when selling into some of the world’s most regulated industries.

sessions.title: Workshop 9 - From Prototype to Production: Building, Securing, and Scaling AI Agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.description:
Building an AI agent is the easy part. Getting it to production — authorized, observable, debuggable, and scalable — is the real engineering challenge. In this hands-on workshop, AWS Solutions Architects and specialists walk you through the key building blocks of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll scaffold an agent with the AgentCore CLI, connect it to tools (MCP servers, APIs, knowledge bases), wire up identity-aware access control, and deploy it — all within a provided AWS sandbox environment and without managing infrastructure. Bring your curiosity and your laptop — whether you work with LangChain, Strands SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, or your own framework, you'll leave with practical, hands-on experience building agents that are ready to evolve toward production. This is not a demo. You will build, break, and debug.

Level: Intermediate to Advanced (300–400), structured in progressive modules with guided support — beginners can follow along while experienced builders push into advanced patterns (agent runtime deployment, multi-tool orchestration with authentication, MCP server integration, IAM-backed access policies, production observability and tracing). Recommended: basic Python and familiarity with AWS core services (IAM, Lambda).

For: software engineers, AI/ML engineers, platform engineers, cloud architects, DevOps/SRE practitioners, and technical founders building AI agent systems.

sessions.title: Workshop 10 - Tether
sessions.description: To be announced...

sessions.title: Fireside 1 - From Dating Fatigue to AI Saturation: Why People Are Coming Back to Real Life
sessions.description:
Dating apps removed rejection, not loneliness. AI removed friction, not the need to be known.

Maxime Barbier built Timeleft on the opposite bet: put strangers around a dinner table in 200 cities worldwide, and make the awkward part the point. In this fireside he argues that friction is a feature, that restaurants have become the last piece of social infrastructure we have left, and that the harder an experience is to outsource to a model, the more it is worth doing yourself.

Booking gives you a room. Skyscanner gives you a flight. Timeleft gives you a human.

A deliberately contrarian counterweight to the rest of the programme, on loneliness, third places, and what we quietly lose to LLMs.

sessions.title: Demo 15 - Beyond the Pilot: How to Give an AI Employee a Real Job
sessions.description: It is easy to build an AI that can hold an impressive conversation. It is much harder to give it responsibility for actual work. Using examples from real deployments across restaurants, dental practices and home services, Ryan McManus breaks down the anatomy of an AI employee: the job it owns, the information it needs, the systems it can access, the decisions it is allowed to make, and the moments when it should hand work back to a human.

sessions.title: Use Case 7 - AI Built on Trust: Turning Smart Data into Secure Intelligence
sessions.description: Discover how smart, governed data can power AI without compromising security, sovereignty or control. A real-world approach to transforming sensitive information into secure, actionable intelligence.

sessions.title: Panel 10 - Place Your Bets: AI in Gaming, Gambling & Live Entertainment
sessions.description: Gambling, gaming, streaming, live events. AI is rewriting the entire entertainment stack, from iGaming algorithms predicting the next bet, to recommendation engines deciding what 200 million people watch tonight, to computer vision changing how a live show feels. It is one of AI's biggest and fastest-moving commercial playgrounds. Operators and builders on what is genuinely running in production today, where personalisation stops paying and starts costing trust, and whether Europe can build the next generation of entertainment with AI at the core.

sessions.title: Fireside 2 — Agents That Touch Real Money
sessions.description:
Most AI-in-finance sessions are about what could be automated. Sophie Cornay runs Qonto AI, a team of ten shipping agentic workflows into a live banking product used across Europe: invoice handling, payment tracking, categorisation, real-time cash visibility.

That means agents operating where mistakes cost money and someone has to be accountable for them. This fireside is about the line she drew — what an agent decides, what it never decides, what broke in production, and what actually slows a team down when the product is regulated.

A working account of shipping agents in finance, not a forecast.

sessions.title: Demo 16 - AI in High-Stakes Environments: A Practitioner's Framework for Responsible, Explainable, and Secure Deployment
sessions.description:
Most AI governance conversations happen at the policy level. I want to bring them to the production level, where the decisions are harder and the consequences are real.
I'll walk through how we built and deployed an AI governance framework inside a regulated healthcare technology platform: what alignment with the EU AI Act, Cyber Resilience Act, and ISO 42001 actually looks like in code, architecture, and process, not on paper. What broke. What we had to rebuild. And why "responsible AI" means something very different when a wrong output affects a patient in behavioral health.

sessions.title: Use Case 8 - Building a Voice Agent for Sports Centre Customer Service
sessions.description: IBM & Baskonia Alaves Group present the design and deployment of an AI voice agent for customer service, beginning at the BAKH training and leisure center and built to extend across the group. The session covers the architecture behind the solution, the integration with existing booking and membership systems, and the operational results observed to date. It also addresses the practical challenges of conversational voice in a live environment, the criteria used to decide what the agent handles and what escalates to a human team, and what the initial deployment revealed about scaling further.

sessions.title: Fireside 3 — What AI Companies Actually Charge For
sessions.description:
Per-seat pricing assumes headcount. If the product does the work instead of helping a person do it, what exactly is being sold — and to whom?

Tim Beck, Co-Founder and CEO of BLP Digital, on the monetisation question underneath every AI product decision: seats versus outcomes, what inference costs do to gross margin, and which pricing models are quietly breaking.

A commercial conversation, not a product one.

sessions.title: Fireside 4 — Generative AI at Consumer Scale
sessions.description:
Shipping a generative feature to professionals is a product problem. Shipping it to a very large consumer base is an engineering, cost and quality problem at the same time.

Artavazd Mehrabyan, Co-Founder and CTO of Picsart, on what changes when your users aren't experts, your inference bill is a line item on the P&L, and the feature has to work the first time or it doesn't get used again.

What consumers adopted, what was built and ignored, and what the engineering org had to become.

sessions.title: Keynote 28 - The Last Mile of Model Accuracy: Agent-Driven Federated Learning for Unseen Domains
sessions.description:
Every AI/ML vendor ships a model that hits its benchmark and then watches it underperform in the field. The customer’s domain is different from the training distribution, and it keeps moving. It shows up everywhere — medical imaging, fintech, anti-fraud, identity and many others — and today it’s closed by guesswork: hunt for more data, retrain blind, repeat over weeks. The vendor is diagnosing a domain it cannot see.

I’ll show what changes when an agent runs where the data already lives: it diagnoses what actually shifted and turns that into a targeted federated fine-tuning plan, without the vendor losing its own baseline.

Two real deployments ground it — one in medical technology, one in anti-spoofing for identity — plus what it takes to make this work, and where it still breaks.

sessions.title: Closing D1: El Ecosistema de IA de Cataluña: Cooperación, Talento y Soluciones de Valor Real
sessions.description:
La Digital Catalonia Alliance (DCA), una iniciativa de la Generalitat de Catalunya impulsada por el Centro de Investigación e Innovación i2CAT, reúne a más de 800 empresas de tecnología digital avanzada. En esta ocasión, empresas innovadoras de la comunidad DCA-IA hablarán sobre cómo impulsar un ecosistema de Inteligencia Artificial dinámico, competitivo e interconectado.

La sesión profundizará en casos de uso reales, proyectos piloto y la visión estratégica del sector en Cataluña, destacando el talento y la capacidad del ecosistema local para liderar la tecnología del futuro y mostrando cómo la colaboración local y la diversidad de capacidades permiten abordar retos complejos con agilidad y excelencia.

sessions.title: Fireside 5 - AI in Regulated Industries: Booster or Barrier?
Keynote 29 - Beyond the AI Noise: Creating Content People Can’t Ignore
sessions.description: In a world where anyone can generate content in seconds, standing out has never been harder - or more valuable. In this talk, Tycho Luijten, founder and CEO of Dapper, shares how brands can create content that cuts through the AI-generated noise: work that's distinctive, human, and impossible to ignore.

sessions.title: Fireside 6 - What's Left to Teach When AI Already Knows the Answer?
sessions.description: Business education was built on transferring knowledge to people who did not have it. That premise is gone. In fifteen minutes, EU Business School takes on what a degree is actually worth now, which skills survive contact with AI, and whether institutions selling multi-year programmes can move fast enough to stay honest with the students paying for them.

sessions.title: Keynote 30 - The intelligence of digital twins: AI to help protect cultural heritage
sessions.description:
Since it was founded in 2013, Iconem has leveraged the latest innovations to document heritage sites under threat, from conflict zones to UNESCO World Heritage sites, turning raw data from the field into precise 3D models at a scale and speed no other process could match. 
This talk retraces that journey: how cultural heritage digitization and AI became inseparable from the start, and how the company's ongoing R&D pushes further, enriching these models into spatialized knowledge systems and intimate,  immersive experiences for all. 
Alongside the technical path, expect a visual journey through some of the most striking digital twins produced to date, and a look at what AI still has to offer a field where what is lost cannot be recaptured.

sessions.title: Keynote 32 - In Medio Stat AI: Governing Artificial Intelligence in a Fragmented World
sessions.description:
Artificial intelligence is global, but the rules governing it are increasingly fragmented. This keynote distinguishes regulation, which establishes legal boundaries, from governance, which makes responsibility operational through real authority, oversight, evidence and accountability.
Comparing the different priorities shaping AI in Europe, the United States and China, Luana Lo Piccolo argues that governance is becoming essential geopolitical and innovation infrastructure. She introduces a practical framework based on five principles - Purpose, Power, Proof, Participation and Portability - to help organisations govern AI responsibly across changing technologies and jurisdictions.
Governance is not the brake on innovation. It is the steering system that allows innovation to endure.

sessions.title: Demo 17 - From Digital Twins to Biological Twins: Modeling Human Life with AI
sessions.description: You can measure your biology. The hard part is knowing if anything you did actually changed it. Astel Allame will show live what that looks like in practice at NutriCheck: 4 drops of blood collected at home, thousands of molecular signals and biomarkers turned into your biological twin. The model runs on one person, with everyone as their own reference, to target the right nutrition, supplementation and lifestyle interventions, and make preventive health truly accessible, measurable and actionable.

sessions.title: Keynote 31 - AI to keep Europe Safe
sessions.description: A Keynote from Airbus Defense and Space

sessions.title: Panel 11 - Creativity at Machine Speed: GenAI in Film, Media & Design
sessions.description: Video models broke through — now what? Leaders from film, broadcast and design on hybrid AI workflows, creator compensation, and where human craft still wins.

sessions.title: Workshop 11 - Build your AI Search workflows. Data-backed optimisation with Surfer MCP
sessions.description:
Hands-on session.

For over a year Surfer's Data Science team has been running experiments on how AI search picks its sources. Across datasets of up to 289,105 URLs, on ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI surfaces. We open with what those experiments found, including the parts that contradict what most people still optimise for.

Then we build. You connect Surfer to your own agent over MCP, and we work through three things: where a brand actually stands in AI answers, how to turn one gap into a piece of work, and how to make that repeat every week without running it by hand.

You leave with a working setup, a report you generated in the room on real data, and a prompt pack that reproduces all of it against your own brand.

Workspace access is provided in the room. The agent subscription is yours to bring.

sessions.title: Workshop 12 - AI for Clarity: Turning Technical Complexity into Stories People Act On
sessions.description:
It’s a practical session showing how AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, etc.) can help professionals remove complexity and create accurate decision narratives. It includes a live demo so people can see the transformation happening in real time.

Given the mix of technical and business audiences at the summit last year, I think this will work well with:
• data and analytics teams that want bigger impact with their insights
• AI technical teams that need to remove jargon when communicating with business colleagues
• business leaders trying to get better engagement from their presentations

sessions.title: Keynote 34 - Beyond Upskilling: Rebuilding Identity in the Age of AI
sessions.description:
Everyone talks about the exponential curve of AI. Almost no one talks about the flat line next to it: the human capacity to adapt.

That gap is already splitting organizations into two populations and triggering something deeper than a skills shortage: an identity crisis. Fear, loss of bearings, resistance as a survival reflex.

Upskilling won't fix this. You can't train your way out of an identity transition.

This keynote introduces The Soft Architecture: an experimental approach for rebuilding professional identity in a transition no one has a map for. If you lead people through change, this is a different kind of conversation.

sessions.title: Keynote 33 - AI Agents: from Zero to Corporate Hero
sessions.description: What changes when AI stops being something we ask for advice and starts carrying out meaningful parts of a workflow? In this talk, we'll explore the most impactful AI agent workflows we've introduced across our companies, from work automation to data analytics, how they fundamentally changed the way we work, and the many lessons we learned along the way.

sessions.title: Hands-On Workshop: Building Agents with Google Antigravity (Bring Your Laptop), by Google Cloud
sessions.description: Step into the future of autonomous software engineering in this 90-minute hands-on lab challenge. Take command with Google Antigravity as you solve real-world tasks - moving from rapid terminal refactoring to orchestrating autonomous multi-agent swarms that execute tools, browse the web, and build software alongside you. (Please bring your laptop!)

sessions.title: Demo 18 - How to Use AI to Grow Your B2B Revenue
sessions.description:
I’ll show you how to use AI to win clients and grow revenue.

Using Claude Code, ColdIQ, Prospeo, and other tools, I’ll build a complete B2B growth system live. You’ll see how to find ideal customers, identify decision-makers, enrich contacts, and launch personalized outreach.

Whether you’re a startup looking for your first customers or a large B2B company ready to accelerate growth, this session is for you.

Bonus: I’ll show you how to use the same system for fundraising. It’s the exact system we used to help a Swiss client raise $5 million.

Real tools. Real workflows. Real growth.

sessions.title: Keynote 36 - How to Build Human Capability as AI Gets Smarter
sessions.description:
AI is making us faster, more productive, and more capable. But there is a question hiding behind those gains: Are we becoming more capable—or simply more capable with AI?

As organizations race to deploy copilots, agents, and increasingly autonomous systems, Don Kilburg argues that leaders need to pay attention to another critical asset: Cognitive Capital—the human capacity for judgment, critical thinking, learning, creativity, adaptability, and wisdom.

In this keynote, Kilburg explores the Capacity Shadow: the potentially hidden gap between what people can accomplish with AI and what they remain capable of doing without it. Emerging research suggests that AI-assisted performance and independent human capability can diverge—and, importantly, that how we design human-AI interaction can change the outcome.

Kilburg introduces Cognitive System Design, a practical approach to building AI-enabled organizations that don’t just maximize today’s performance, but deliberately develop the human capabilities they will need tomorrow.

The goal isn’t less AI. It’s better human-AI systems.

You have an AI strategy. Do you have a cognitive strategy?

sessions.title: Keynote 35 - ¿Qué AI en el Banco de España?
sessions.description: Exposición sobre cómo se usa la IA en el Banco de España.

sessions.title: Panel 12 - From Scan to Startup: AI Healthcare in the Real World
sessions.description: AI already reads scans, catches cancers earlier and reshapes drug discovery — but it learned from biased data. Clinicians, founders and investors on what works today and what we must fix.

sessions.title: Keynote 38 - The rise of Hybrid Builders - The profiles shaping the next phase of AI transformation.
sessions.description:
Organizations have never invested more in AI. Yet many still struggle to turn these investments into a measurable business impact. The missing piece is not technology, it is people.  As AI becomes part of everyday work, a new profile is emerging: professionals who understand business challenges, know how to build with AI and help organizations adopt new ways of working. At Mantu, we call them Hybrid Builders. 
This keynote explores why the next phase of AI transformation will be defined not only by technology, but by the organizations capable of developing the people who can turn AI into business value.

sessions.title: Demo 19 - From Reactive to Proactive: Building AI Agents that Anticipate Customer Needs
sessions.description:
We’re collecting more data than ever, building powerful chatbots, designing complex workflows but users still just want ONE thing: to get what they need with as little effort as possible.
In this talk, we’ll explore how AI agents can help bridge that gap: not by asking users to give more, but by leveraging what we already know to deliver faster, smarter, and more intuitive experiences. In the live demo of an agentic assistant we will see a shift from reactive to proactive behavior. We will discuss common pitfalls when building agentic systems and tap into their evaluation for large scale solutions.

sessions.title: Keynote 37 - AI in Sales real life. What works, what does not work
sessions.description: Real life examples of AI applied to our Revenue Department. Best and worse practices on what works and where we failed badly.

sessions.title: Keynote 40 - Cybersecurity
sessions.description: To be announced...

sessions.title: Keynote 39 - MLOps
sessions.description: To be announced...

sessions.title: Demo 20 - Inside the architecture: Building a production-ready AI venture
sessions.description:
What does it actually take to move from AI prototype to production-grade product? In this technical deep dive, Michael van Lier unpacks the architecture behind one of Builders’ AI ventures — from model selection and orchestration layers to data pipelines, infra decisions, and governance.

Rather than theory, this session explores real design trade-offs, scalability challenges, and the hard calls that shaped the product. Ideal for technical founders, product leaders, and engineers who want to understand what breaks, what scales, and what matters when building AI systems in the real world.

sessions.title: Panel 13 - Energy Resilience & AI Climate Adaptation
sessions.description: Two very different things get called climate AI: predicting and pricing risk, and keeping physical systems running when the weather breaks them. This panel holds both and stays honest about which is which. What hazard models can actually forecast at asset level, what insurers and investors will underwrite on the back of it, and what happens when AI's own compute becomes one of the fastest growing loads on the same grid everyone is trying to protect.

sessions.title: Workshop 13 - From Design to Live Campaign: Marketing Automation Rebuilt Around AI Agents
sessions.description:
Marketing automation has a production bottleneck. Turning a design into an inbox-proof email takes days of specialist work. Wiring it into the platform (personalization, data extensions, automations, journeys) takes days more. Every campaign pays that tax again.

We rebuilt that workflow around AI agents, and we'll show the whole thing running: a Figma design goes in, production-grade email-safe HTML comes out, validated across real inboxes, and the email, the AMPscript personalization, the Data Extensions, the Automations and the Journey get built inside the marketing platform. The specialist stays in command throughout, setting the intent and approving at gates the agents cannot pass on their own.

Full autonomy is not the goal. In a discipline where a bad send is irreversible, it shouldn't be. Orchestration is.

Then we hand the controls to the room: ask for a change, and we run it live."

Requirements:
No requirements. No laptop, no setup, no accounts.

This is a demo-led session, not a build-along. The workflow runs on our own repository and against live client platforms, so we can't hand out the environment, and building the full pipeline live would eat well past our slot. What you get instead is the complete workflow end to end, plus a live segment where you call the changes and we operate the system in front of you.

No technical background required.

sessions.title: Workshop 14 - Can AI Replace Your Buyer Interviews? Building Robust Synthetic Personas
sessions.description:
B2B market research has always been the industry's hardest nut to crack: small sample sizes, gatekept buyers, slow timelines, and insights that go stale before you can act on them. In this talk, Kate Busby breaks down how AI-generated synthetic personas are changing the equation, not as a shortcut, but as a rigorous, repeatable process.
Kate walks through the full methodology: how to construct synthetic personas that actually reflect real buyer behavior, the data fidelity checks that separate a useful model from a hallucinated one, and the validation loops needed to trust the output enough to act on it. She'll share hard-won lessons from running this process against real B2B audiences, where it holds up, where it breaks, and how to know the difference.
Attendees will leave with a practical framework for building synthetic personas that go beyond guesswork, giving growth and marketing teams faster, cheaper, and more reliable access to the qualitative insight B2B research has always struggled to deliver at scale.

sessions.title: Keynote 42 - SaaSApocalypse in the era of AI Agent
sessions.description:
AI agents are rewriting the rules for the entire SaaS industry. Tools we paid monthly subscriptions for can now be recreated by an agent in minutes — and increasingly, users don't want to click through an interface at all; they just want to issue a command. Is this the end of SaaS as we know it?
In this talk I'll show why the classic "feature-for-subscription" model is running out of road, and what that means for anyone building software today. I'll speak as a practitioner — drawing on lessons from running my own SaaS products — about shifting our thinking from "ship more features" to "build value an agent can't replicate."
A central theme will be sovereignty: in a world where your product talks to AI agents and your data flows through models you don't own, who actually controls the customer relationship, the data, and the value? I'll argue that digital and data sovereignty become the real moat — the thing that separates companies that get commoditized by agents from those that own their future.
You'll leave with a concrete map: which business models are most exposed, where new opportunities are opening up, and how to prepare your product today for a world where the first user of your app is an AI agent, not a human.

sessions.title: Keynote 41 - Private AI Exchange: Private by Design. Public by Choice.
sessions.description:
Build the base in Private AI for core workloads that matters. Rent the spike in Public AI.
Digital Realty provides the meeting place for both.

sessions.title: Debate 3 — Sovereign AI or Surrender? Should Europe Stop Outsourcing Its AI Future?
sessions.description: Europe is building 13 AI Factories, funding Mistral and Aleph Alpha, demanding open weights, and writing the world's strictest AI law. Yet 90% of European AI compute still runs on AWS, Azure and GCP, and the foundation model leaderboards are American and Chinese. So is sovereign AI the project of the decade for European strategic autonomy — or an expensive industrial-policy fantasy that taxes EU founders without producing winners? One debater says Europe must stop renting its future. The other says we already lost — partner up and accept it.

sessions.title: Demo 21 - From Dashboards to Decisions: Building AI-Powered Analytics on Top of Modern Data Platforms
sessions.description:
AI is transforming how businesses interact with data, but successful AI initiatives start long before an LLM is introduced. Without reliable data foundations, even the most advanced models become expensive sources of incorrect answers.

This session explores how modern analytics platforms can evolve from traditional dashboards into AI-powered decision-support systems. Using a real-world architecture journey, we compare fragmented reporting environments with a centralized data platform built around a data warehouse, semantic layer, and self-service analytics.

We will discuss why data architecture determines the practical limits of AI adoption, how to design data flows that create trust in analytical results, and how agent-based interfaces can make data more accessible to business users. Rather than replacing analysts, AI agents act as a natural interface between people and data—automating routine investigations, accelerating insight discovery, and helping organizations answer questions such as “Why did sales decline last month?” in seconds instead of hours.

The session concludes with a live demonstration of an LLM-powered analytics agent working on top of a governed data platform.

sessions.title: Keynote 43 - The 10x Enterprise: Scaling AI Platforms for Compound Value
sessions.description:
While base models advance with every quarterly update, most enterprise AI agents remain trapped in proof-of-concept purgatory. The core bottleneck is no longer intelligence, which can be easily rented off the shelf, but the non-rentable foundation: deep domain context, persistent memory, action rights, continuous evaluation, and real-world agent governance.

This infrastructure represents the custom platform layer every organization must own to unlock true enterprise scale. In this session, Arvand breaks down the architectural blueprint for the next-generation AI platform, outlining what to rent, what to build, and precisely where to start to drive compound value.

sessions.title: Panel 14 - Money, Reinvented: AI Agents, Stablecoins & the Future of Finance
sessions.description: Agents that pay, tokenized rails, banks racing fintechs to deploy AI under the world's strictest rules. The people building the future of money on what's real and what's next.

sessions.title: Keynote 44 - Your User Is Asleep at 3am. What Is Your Agent Allowed to Do?
sessions.description:
Almost every agent at this conference assumes there's someone there to answer it. Ours often can't be: the traveller is in the air, asleep, or standing at a gate at three in the morning.
That changes what you have to build. A booking isn't a transaction — it's a workflow that can break for weeks. Something has to hold the problem until it's resolved, know what it's allowed to do without asking, and know when to wake a human instead.
Tyler Foster, CPTO at BizAway, on how a trip is modelled so that one delayed flight invalidates everything downstream of it, where the line sits between what an agent decides alone and what it escalates to a person, and what six months of defect data across two codebases decided about how much we were willing to let it do unattended.

sessions.title: Deploying AI Across the Workforce with Gemini Enterprise, by Google Cloud
sessions.description: Move beyond passive search and rigid assistants. In this session, you will discover how any employee can build custom AI agents, automate workflows across your existing stack, and establish the governance layer needed to scale securely across the organization with Gemini Enterprise

sessions.title: Demo 22 - Leverage AI to Build MVPs fast
sessions.description:
Compress your time-to-market by building and shipping functional MVPs in days using AI coding assistants, code generation, and rapid prototyping pipelines.

Focus on validating demand early and iterating fast while adopting AI-native execution to automate development workflows and significantly increase output. At the same time, design with scalability in mind from day one so your product can grow without rework.
This is an end-to-end approach to build, test, and scale products at startup speed.

sessions.title: Keynote 45 - Greener AI is possible: the decisions behind Ecosia's AI products
sessions.description: Ecosia is a search engine owned by a foundation. It can't be sold, it will never go public, and 100% of its profits go to climate action. We built generative AI without pretending the costs weren't real but knowing Greener AI was not impossible. The decisions behind a lighter-footprint AI and a genuine European competitor to Big Tech.

sessions.title: Keynote 47 - AEO (Answer Engine Optimization): The Critical Growth Channel
sessions.description: AI Visibility (appearing in AI recommendations) is imperative amidst the current decline in search traffic. Understand the nature of the moment and what you can do to take advantage of it.

sessions.title: Demo 23 - AI for data analytics
sessions.description: In this session we will cover how the data analytics has been impacted by AI and get a glimpse of a possible future in agentic analytics.

sessions.title: Keynote 46 - The AI Enterprise Value Gap
sessions.description:
AI capabilities are growing at an unprecedented pace, with a never ending flow of new models that beat every single benchmark. 

However, enterprise value barely reflects this, and most AI initiatives fail to reach production and provide measurable impact, generating a gap between the technological capabilities available, and how much enterprises benefit from them.

This talk explores why that gap exists, why it's no longer a technology problem but an execution problem, and how Aily Labs, with their Decision Intelligence App turns intelligence into faster decisions, better operations, and real P&L impact

sessions.title: Panel 15 - Who's Really Deciding? Human Agency in the Age of AI
sessions.description: An algorithm nudges what your kid reads before bed. A hiring filter decides who a recruiter never sees. A health app flags what's wrong before your doctor does. None of this is speculative — it's this year's default UX. As AI mediates more of daily life — work, health, relationships, money, parenting — how much control do people actually keep, and how much do they just assume they still have? Voices from product, psychology, and policy separate where human agency genuinely holds from where it's already quietly gone. 40 minutes.

sessions.title: Keynote 49 - Tokens, Latency, Sovereignty: The Physics Pulling AI to the Edge
Keynote 48 - Dataiku
